dimension: Form axis (Kabsch RMSD <= 1 A) and the placement-vs-form decomposition under the nearest-copy convention
summary: (1) PoseBusters semantics, read at posebusters/modules/rmsd.py:52-70: check_rmsd computes rmsds, kabsch_rmsds and intercentroids for EVERY conformer of mol_true, then with the default choose_by="rmsd" takes i = argmin(rmsds) and reports kabsch_rmsd = kabsch_rmsds[i]. The Kabsch value therefore FOLLOWS the conformer that minimised the in-place RMSD; it is not an independent minimum. The multi-conformer mol_true comes from tools/loading.py:121 -> _load_and_combine_mols (:158-166), which AddConformer()s every SDF record onto the first "without checking identity or atom order"; I verified all 138 multi-copy ids in the 303 have identical element sequence and bond list across records, so that path is safe on this benchmark. Empirically (24,486 multi-copy poses, six arms) the PoseBusters multi-conformer kabsch equals the kabsch of the in-place-argmin copy to 5e-5 A and differs from the independent min-over-copies in 13,247 poses (max 3.46 A). (2) Kabsch against the nearest copy computed for all 24,486 multi-copy poses of the six arms (13,328 with nearest_copy_is_ref False) plus 20,587 for the five other Table 1 arms, via the thesis loaders, reassign_template and ppc.posebusters_rmsd(pose, copy) per copy; kabsch_ref reproduces bestfit_rmsd to 8.9e-16 A on every row including the 50 single-copy check poses and 11,158 multi-copy nearest==ref rows; recomputed sym_rmsd reproduces rmsd/rmsd_nearest_copy to 5e-10 A and pb_rmsd_ref reproduces pb_rmsd to 3e-11 A. Files: wf/nearest_copy_kabsch.csv, wf/nearest_copy_kabsch_extra_arms.csv, wf/per_pose_two_conventions.csv (53,651 rows with kabsch_nearest, kabsch_min_all, pb_rmsd_nearest, cd_nearest). (3) All reference-convention values reproduce exactly (Table 1 cells, 160/133/55, 74.3/74.6/95.4/97.0, 47/46, 6,169/2,329). Under nearest-copy with form following the in-place copy: Table 1 Form column barely moves (AutoDock* 227/2,836/31.6% -> 227/2,823/31.5%; DiffDock* 237/3,903/43.4% -> 236/3,887/43.2%; EquiBind* 200/2,661/29.3% -> 199/2,661/29.3%) and three arms LOSE one form complex, because the copy a pose sits on can be a slightly different conformer than the reference; the combined (triple) column jumps (AutoDock raw/gnina 164/160 -> 178/175 complexes, 221/221 -> 324/325 poses; DiffDock* 138 -> 148, 1,227 -> 1,516; EquiBind* 55 -> 57). Triple-gate top-15 selection: AutoDock* 160 -> 175, DiffDock smina 133 -> 144 vs gnina 132 -> 143 (smina still carried, 1,031 vs 1,022 poses, seven discordant, three gnina-only), EquiBind gnina 55 -> 57 vs smina 46 -> 48. Kabsch recovery at best-of-top-30 is unchanged at the quoted precision: 74.3/74.6 at 1 A and 95.4/97.0 at 2 A; rank-1 52.5/52.1/33.3 unchanged; EquiBind top-30 54.1 -> 53.8; 26 of 90 Table 26 Kabsch cells move by 0.3-0.7 pp; form McNemar AutoDock vs DiffDock 47/46, 30/31, 25/26 -> 48/47, 30/32, 25/26 (p_holm stays 1.000). The H.4 / Figure 4 decomposition inputs (_form_components: inplace = pb_rmsd, form = bestfit_rmsd, plus the 8 A centroid trim) ALL move for the 13,328 flipped poses and the cohort grows: 6,169 -> 7,565 PB-valid near-site poses at top-15 (2,329 -> 2,854 clipped), rank-1 coverage 62.7/54.1/47.2% -> 82.2/73.9/51.2%, all 117 Table 27 cells change (AutoDock rank-1 in-place median 1.490 -> 1.376, top-15 5.043 -> 4.922, drift +3.55 unchanged; DiffDock drift +0.46 -> +0.53; EquiBind +1.09 -> +0.96). The validity-within-near-native strata of Appendix H.4 grow from 319/1,715/498 to 451/2,169/515 poses. (4) Form should FOLLOW the in-place nearest copy, as PoseBusters does: it keeps one comparator per pose so in-place^2 = placement^2 + form^2 remains meaningful, and it is what redock.yml load_all produces. The independent min-over-copies differs at the 1 A gate on 271 of 24,486 multi-copy poses, never loses a pose (by construction) and raises DiffDock top-30 1 A recovery to 75.2%, rank-1 DiffDock/EquiBind to 52.5/34.0%, DiffDock top-15 triple to 146 vs 144, and Table 1 form complexes to 227/238/200; the cost is that form then credits conformational heterogeneity between chains rather than the copy the pose actually recovered. Because the follow convention loses one form complex in three arms (149 poses lost, 91 gained), the "no complex loses" statement of the M2 sensitivity arm is true for near-nativeness but NOT for the Form block and must not be carried over.

decisions.question: Should the form (Kabsch) value follow the copy chosen by the in-place minimum, or be minimised independently over all copies?
options: Follow the in-place nearest copy (PoseBusters choose_by='rmsd' semantics; one comparator per pose; keeps in-place^2 = placement^2 + form^2 on a single copy). Effects vs today: Table 1 form complexes 225/227/224/236/235/186/192/199 for the eight main rows (three arms lose one complex, 149 poses lost, 91 gained); headline 74.3/74.6/95.4/97.0 and 52.5/52.1/33.3 unchanged; EquiBind top-30 54.1 -> 53.8; DiffDock top-15 triple 144 vs gnina 143.

Independent minimum over copies (never loses a pose; credits the best-matching deposited conformer regardless of where the pose sits). Effects: Table 1 form complexes 225/227/227/238/236/188/195/200; DiffDock top-30 1 A 75.2, rank-1 52.5, EquiBind rank-1 34.0 / top-30 54.1; DiffDock top-15 triple 146 vs 144; verdict differs from follow on 271 of 24,486 multi-copy poses; breaks the single-copy quadrature for the 13,248 poses where the copies differ.
decisions.recommendation: Follow the in-place nearest copy. It is what the upstream tool does, it is the only rule under which placement = sqrt(in-place^2 - form^2) refers to one physical comparator, and the headline form numbers are unchanged under it. Disclose explicitly that the Form block can lose a complex (three rows drop by one), so the 'no complex loses' statement stays confined to near-nativeness.

decisions.question: Redefine the existing columns (bestfit_rmsd, pb_rmsd, pb_kabsch_rmsd, centroid_dist, rmsd) as the nearest-copy values and add *_refcopy secondaries, or add new *_nearest columns and leave the old names as the single-instance values?
options: Redefine primary names; add bestfit_rmsd_refcopy, pb_rmsd_refcopy, rmsd_refcopy, centroid_dist_refcopy, plus nearest_copy_index and n_copies.

Keep old names single-instance; add *_nearest columns and rename every reader (_form_components, aggregate_pose_validity_cascade, aggregate_topn_within_thresholds callers, _filmstrip_cohorts, filmstrip_rank1_top5_top15.py, thesis_assertions.py x3, yaml metric mapping, thesis_endpoint_diagnostics.py).

Fourteen scripts and the assertion harness read bestfit_rmsd and rmsd by name; the secondary column is what the plan calls for anyway, and the gate documentation in thesis_assertions.py:18-19 and the yaml comment at :57-58 then need only a wording change.

decisions.question: Who chooses the copy: the thesis symmetry_rmsd (loop over copies, pass the chosen single copy to check_rmsd) or PoseBusters' own multi-conformer check_rmsd (load_all, CalcRMS argmin)?
options: Thesis symmetry_rmsd picks the copy for rmsd, then pb_rmsd/kabsch/centroid/torsions are computed against that same copy (what wf/nearest_copy_kabsch.csv did).
Hand PoseBusters the combined multi-conformer mol_true and let its CalcRMS argmin pick; compute symmetry_rmsd separately as min over copies.
decisions.recommendation: Thesis symmetry_rmsd picks. CalcRMS and symmetry_rmsd differ by up to 1.295 A on individual poses in the six arms, so letting each engine pick independently can put rmsd and bestfit_rmsd on different copies for rare poses and break the decomposition; a single explicit selection index avoids that and is what the M2 probe already validated to 5e-10 A.
